verses.zh: 耶和华差遣拿单去见大卫。拿单到了大卫那里，对他说：「在一座城里有两个人：一个是富户，一个是穷人。
verses.en: So the Lord sent Nathan[NOTE:1] to David. When he came to David,[NOTE:2] Nathan[NOTE:3] said,[NOTE:4] “There were two men in a certain city, one rich and the other poor.
notes: A few medieval Hebrew mss, the LXX, and the Syriac Peshitta add “the prophet.” The words are included in a few modern English version (e.g., TEV, CEV, NLT).
Heb “him”; the referent (David) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “he”; the referent (Nathan) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
The Hebrew text repeats “to him.”

verses.zh: 富户有许多牛群羊群；
verses.en: The rich man had a great many flocks and herds.

verses.zh: 穷人除了所买来养活的一只小母羊羔之外，别无所有。羊羔在他家里和他儿女一同长大，吃他所吃的，喝他所喝的，睡在他怀中，在他看来如同女儿一样。
verses.en: But the poor man had nothing except for a little lamb he had acquired. He raised it, and it grew up alongside him and his children.[NOTE:1] It used to[NOTE:2] eat his food,[NOTE:3] drink from his cup, and sleep in his arms.[NOTE:4] It was just like a daughter to him.
notes: Heb “his sons.”
The three Hebrew imperfect verbal forms in this sentence have a customary nuance; they describe past actions that were repeated or typical.
Heb “from his morsel.”
Heb “and on his chest [or perhaps, “lap”] it would lie.”

verses.zh: 有一客人来到这富户家里；富户舍不得从自己的牛群羊群中取一只预备给客人吃，却取了那穷人的羊羔，预备给客人吃。」
verses.en: “When a traveler arrived at the rich man’s home,[NOTE:1] he did not want to use one of his own sheep or cattle to feed[NOTE:2] the traveler who had come to visit him.[NOTE:3] Instead, he took the poor man’s lamb and cooked[NOTE:4] it for the man who had come to visit him.”
notes: Heb “came to the rich man.” In the translation “arrived at the rich man’s home” has been used for stylistic reasons.
Heb “and he refused to take from his flock and from his herd to prepare [a meal] for.”
Heb “who had come to him” (also a second time later in this verse). The word “visit” has been supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons and for clarity.
Heb “and prepared.”

verses.zh: 大卫就甚恼怒那人，对拿单说：「我指着永生的耶和华起誓，行这事的人该死！
verses.en: Then David became very angry at this man. He said to Nathan, “As surely as the Lord lives, the man who did this deserves to die![NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the man doing this [is] a son of death.” See 1 Sam 20:31 for another use of this expression, which must mean “he is as good as dead” or “he deserves to die,” as 1 Sam 20:32 makes clear.

verses.zh: 他必偿还羊羔四倍；因为他行这事，没有怜恤的心。」
verses.en: Because he committed this cold-hearted crime, he must pay for the lamb four times over!”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the lamb he must repay fourfold because he did this thing and because he did not have compassion.”tc With the exception of the Lucianic recension, the Old Greek translation has here “sevenfold” rather than “fourfold,” a reading that S. R. Driver thought probably to be the original reading (S. R. Driver, Notes on the Hebrew Text and the Topography of the Books of Samuel, 291). However, Exod 22:1 [21:37 HT] specifies fourfold repayment for a stolen sheep, which is consistent with 2 Sam 12:6. Some mss of the Targum and the Syriac Peshitta exaggerate the idea to “fortyfold.”

verses.zh: 拿单对大卫说：「你就是那人！耶和华―以色列的　神如此说：『我膏你作以色列的王，救你脱离扫罗的手。
verses.en: Nathan said to David, “You are that man! This is what the Lord God of Israel has said: ‘I chose[NOTE:1] you to be king over Israel and I rescued you from the hand of Saul.
notes: Heb “anointed.”

verses.zh: 我将你主人的家业赐给你，将你主人的妻交在你怀里，又将以色列和犹大家赐给你；你若还以为不足，我早就加倍地赐给你。
verses.en: I gave you your master’s house, and put your master’s wives into your arms.[NOTE:1] I also gave you the house of Israel and Judah. And if all that somehow seems insignificant, I would have given you so much more as well!
notes: Heb “and the wives of your lord into your chest [or “lap”].” The words “I put” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons and for clarification.

verses.zh: 你为甚么藐视耶和华的命令，行他眼中看为恶的事呢？你借亚扪人的刀杀害赫人乌利亚，又娶了他的妻为妻。
verses.en: Why have you shown contempt for the Lord’s decrees[NOTE:1] by doing evil in my[NOTE:2] sight? You have struck down Uriah the Hittite with the sword and you have taken his wife to be your own wife! You have killed him with the sword of the Ammonites.
notes: Or “word, message.” The “word of the Lord” sometimes refers to a prophetic message from God and sometimes to his past revelation. Here it refers to the Lord’s laws which David has violated.
So the Qere; the Kethib has “his.”

verses.zh: 你既藐视我，娶了赫人乌利亚的妻为妻，所以刀剑必永不离开你的家。』
verses.en: So now the sword will never depart from your house. For you have despised me by taking the wife of Uriah the Hittite as your own!’

verses.zh: 耶和华如此说：『我必从你家中兴起祸患攻击你；我必在你眼前把你的妃嫔赐给别人，他在日光之下就与她们同寝。
verses.en: This is what the Lord has said: ‘I am about to bring disaster on you[NOTE:1] from inside your own household![NOTE:2] Right before your eyes I will take your wives and hand them over to your companion.[NOTE:3] He will go to bed with[NOTE:4] your wives in broad daylight![NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “raise up against you disaster.”
Heb “house” (so NAB, NRSV); NCV, TEV, CEV “family.”
Or “friend.”
Heb “will lie down with.” The verb שָׁכַב (shakhav) “to lie down” can be a euphemism for going to bed for sexual relations.
Heb “in the eyes of this sun.”

verses.zh: 你在暗中行这事，我却要在以色列众人面前，日光之下，报应你。』」
verses.en: Although you have acted in secret, I will do this thing before all Israel, and in broad daylight.’”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and before the sun.”

verses.zh: 大卫对拿单说：「我得罪耶和华了！」拿单说：「耶和华已经除掉你的罪，你必不至于死。
verses.en: Then David exclaimed to Nathan, “I have sinned against the Lord!” Nathan replied to David, “Yes, and the Lord has forgiven[NOTE:1] your sin. You are not going to die.
notes: Heb “removed.”

verses.zh: 只是你行这事，叫耶和华的仇敌大得亵渎的机会，故此，你所得的孩子必定要死。」
verses.en: Nonetheless, because you have treated the Lord with such contempt[NOTE:1] in this matter, the son who has been born to you will certainly die.”
notes: The MT has here “because you have caused the enemies of the Lord to treat the Lord with such contempt.” This is one of the so-called tiqqune sopherim, or “emendations of the scribes.” According to this ancient tradition, the scribes changed the text in order to soften somewhat the negative light in which David was presented. If that is the case, the MT reflects the altered text. The present translation departs from the MT here. Elsewhere the Piel stem of this verb means “treat with contempt,” but never “cause someone to treat with contempt.”

verses.zh: 拿单就回家去了。耶和华击打乌利亚妻给大卫所生的孩子，使他得重病。
verses.en: Then Nathan went to his home. The Lord struck the child that Uriah’s wife had borne to David, and the child became very ill.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and the Lord struck the child…and he was ill.” It is necessary to repeat “the child” in the translation to make clear who became ill, since “the Lord struck the child that Uriah’s wife had borne to David, and he became very ill” could be understood to mean that David himself became ill.

verses.zh: 所以大卫为这孩子恳求　神，而且禁食，进入内室，终夜躺在地上。
verses.en: Then David prayed to[NOTE:1] God for the child and fasted.[NOTE:2] He would even[NOTE:3] go and spend the night lying on the ground.
notes: Heb “sought” or “searched for.”
Heb “and David fasted.”
The three Hebrew verbs that follow in this verse are perfects with prefixed vav. They may describe repeated past actions or actions which accompanied David’s praying and fasting.

verses.zh: 他家中的老臣来到他旁边，要把他从地上扶起来，他却不肯起来，也不同他们吃饭。
verses.en: The elders of his house stood over him and tried to lift him from the ground, but he was unwilling, and refused to eat food with them.

verses.zh: 到第七日，孩子死了。大卫的臣仆不敢告诉他孩子死了，因他们说：「孩子还活着的时候，我们劝他，他尚且不肯听我们的话，若告诉他孩子死了，岂不更加忧伤吗？」
verses.en: On the seventh day the child died. But the servants of David were afraid to inform him that the child had died, for they said, “While the child was still alive he would not listen to us[NOTE:1] when we spoke to him. How can we tell him that the child is dead? He will do himself harm!”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “to our voice.”
Heb “he will do harm.” The object is not stated in the Hebrew text. The statement may be intentionally vague, meaning that he might harm himself or them!

verses.zh: 大卫见臣仆彼此低声说话，就知道孩子死了，问臣仆说：「孩子死了吗？」他们说：「死了。」
verses.en: When David saw that his servants were whispering to one another, he[NOTE:1] realized that the child was dead. So David asked his servants, “Is the child dead?” They replied, “Yes, he’s dead.”
notes: Heb “David.” The name has been replaced in the translation by the pronoun (“he”) for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 大卫就从地上起来，沐浴，抹膏，换了衣裳，进耶和华的殿敬拜；然后回宫，吩咐人摆饭，他便吃了。
verses.en: So David got up from the ground, bathed, put on oil, and changed his clothes. He went to the house of the Lord and worshiped. Then, when he entered his palace, he requested that food be brought to him, and he ate.

verses.zh: 臣仆问他说：「你所行的是甚么意思？孩子活着的时候，你禁食哭泣；孩子死了，你倒起来吃饭。」
verses.en: His servants said to him, “What is this that you have done? While[NOTE:1] the child was still alive, you fasted and wept. Once the child was dead you got up and ate food!”
notes: For the MT בַּעֲבוּר (baʿavur, “for the sake of”) we should probably read בְּעוֹד (beʿod, “while”). See the Lucianic Greek recension, the Syriac Peshitta, and the Targum.

verses.zh: 大卫说：「孩子还活着，我禁食哭泣；因为我想，或者耶和华怜恤我，使孩子不死也未可知。
verses.en: He replied, “While the child was still alive, I fasted and wept because I thought,[NOTE:1] ‘Perhaps[NOTE:2] the Lord will show pity and the child will live.’
notes: Heb “said.”
Heb “Who knows?”

verses.zh: 孩子死了，我何必禁食，我岂能使他返回呢？我必往他那里去，他却不能回我这里来。」
verses.en: But now he is dead. Why should I fast? Am I able to bring him back at this point? I will go to him, but he cannot return to me!”

verses.zh: 大卫安慰他的妻拔示巴，与她同寝，她就生了儿子，给他起名叫所罗门。耶和华也喜爱他，
verses.en: So David comforted his wife Bathsheba. He came to her[NOTE:1] and went to bed with her.[NOTE:2] Later she gave birth to a son, and David[NOTE:3] named him Solomon. Now the Lord loved the child[NOTE:4]
notes: The combination of the verb בּוֹא (boʾ; “to come, enter”) and the preposition אֶל (ʾel; “to”) means “to approach, to come to” (HALOT 1:113). This common expression is also used as a euphemism for coming together for sexual relations. Although some take the phrase to be a graphic depiction of a man actions in sexual relations with a woman, certain factors clarify that it is a euphemism. First, the phrase also describes a woman approaching a man for sexual relations (2 Sam 11:4), a situation where this phrase cannot be explicitly descriptive. Second, the phrase is paired here with שָׁכַב (shakhav), “to lie down,” which only makes sense if the two are complementary (compare also Gen 19:33-34 which uses both verbs of Lot’s daughters, but without the preposition). The verb שָׁכַב can imply lying down for sleep or for sexual relations. When בּוֹא אֶל (boʾ ʾel) is used with שָׁכַב (shakhav), they state the natural progression of approaching and then lying with. Hebrew can use the two together, or either separately, as a euphemism for sexual relations. But if the phrase בּוֹא אֶל were already an explicit depiction of sex, then the latter phrase with שָׁכַב, “to lie with,” would be pointless. So 2 Sam 11:4 and 2 Sam 12:24 are important evidence for how this phrase really works, and it is appropriate to also use euphemisms in translation.
Heb “and he lay with her.” The phrase is a euphemism for sexual relations.

Heb “he”; the referent (David) has been specified in the translation for clarity. While some translations render the pronoun as third person plural (“they”), implying that both David and Bathsheba together named the child, it is likely that the name “Solomon,” which is related to the Hebrew word for “peace” (and may be derived from it) had special significance for David, who would have regarded the birth of a second child to Bathsheba as a confirming sign that God had forgiven his sin and was at peace with him.tc The Kethiv reads “he named” while the Qere reads “she named.”
Heb “him,” referring to the child.

verses.zh: 就藉先知拿单赐他一个名字，叫耶底底亚，因为耶和华爱他。
verses.en: and sent word through Nathan the prophet that he should be named Jedidiah[NOTE:1] for the Lord’s sake.
notes: The name Jedidiah means “loved by the Lord.”

verses.zh: 约押攻取亚扪人的京城拉巴。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] So Joab fought against Rabbah of the Ammonites and captured the royal city.
notes: Here the narrative resumes the battle story that began in 11:1 (see 11:25). The author has interrupted that story to give the related account of David’s sin with Bathsheba and the murder of Uriah. He now returns to the earlier story and brings it to a conclusion.

verses.zh: 约押打发使者去见大卫，说：「我攻打拉巴，取其水城。
verses.en: Joab then sent messengers to David, saying, “I have fought against Rabbah and have captured the water supply of the city.[NOTE:1]
notes: The expression translated the water supply of the city (Heb “the city of the waters”) apparently refers to that part of the fortified city that guarded the water supply of the entire city. Joab had already captured this part of the city, but he now defers to King David for the capture of the rest of the city. In this way the king will receive the credit for this achievement.

verses.zh: 现在你要聚集其余的军兵来，安营围攻这城，恐怕我取了这城，人就以我的名叫这城。」
verses.en: So now assemble the rest of the army[NOTE:1] and besiege the city and capture it. Otherwise I will capture the city and it will be named for me.”
notes: Heb “people.” So also in vv. 29, 31.

verses.zh: 于是大卫聚集众军，往拉巴去攻城，就取了这城，
verses.en: So David assembled all the army and went to Rabbah and fought against it and captured it.

verses.zh: 夺了亚扪人之王所戴的金冠冕（王：或译玛勒堪；玛勒堪就是米勒公，又名摩洛，亚扪族之神名），其上的金子重一他连得，又嵌着宝石。人将这冠冕戴在大卫头上。大卫从城里夺了许多财物，
verses.en: He took the crown of their king[NOTE:1] from his head—it was gold, weighed about 75 pounds,[NOTE:2] and held a precious stone—and it was placed on David’s head. He also took from the city a great deal of plunder.
notes: Part of the Greek tradition wrongly understands Hebrew מַלְכָּם (malkam, “their king”) as a proper name (“Milcom”). Some English versions follow the Greek here, rendering the phrase “the crown of Milcom” (so NRSV; cf. also NAB, CEV). TEV takes this as a reference not to the Ammonite king but to “the idol of the Ammonite god Molech.”
Heb “and its weight [was] a talent of gold.” The weight of this ornamental crown was approximately 75 lbs (34 kg). See P. K. McCarter, II Samuel (AB), 313.

verses.zh: 将城里的人拉出来，放在锯下，或铁耙下，或铁斧下，或叫他经过砖窑（或译：强他们用锯，或用打粮食的铁器，或用铁斧做工，或使在砖窑里服役）；大卫待亚扪各城的居民都是如此。其后，大卫和众军都回耶路撒冷去了。
verses.en: He removed[NOTE:1] the people who were in it and made them labor with saws, iron picks, and iron axes, putting them to work[NOTE:2] at the brick kiln. This was his policy[NOTE:3] with all the Ammonite cities. Then David and all the army returned to Jerusalem.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “brought out.”
Heb “to pass through.”
Heb “and so he would do.”
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
